title: LIV Golf CEO strikes defiant tone, says league is ‘really excited about where we are’
content:
LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil struck a defiant tone on Thursday, arguing that the league is “really excited about where we are” amid reporting that its original funding source is preparing to pull its investment.

O’Neil spoke to Arlo White, part of LIV’s in-house broadcasting team, in a prerecorded segment that aired during television coverage of its first-round event in Mexico City.

“This notion of, do you have to raise money? Probably. Like, this is business, you know? But if we keep the trajectory going the way we are, and the revenue growth going, this is going to be a really good business for a really long time,” O’Neil told White.

It’s a similar message to the one O’Neil delivered in an email to employees Wednesday, when he wrote that “our season continues exactly as planned.”

Two sources briefed on both the email’s contents and its distribution verified its authenticity to The Athletic, on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly.

LIV Golf’s immediate and long-term future were thrown into question amid widespread news reports. Golf industry sources have told The Athletic that the Public Investment Fund, the Saudi Arabian sovereign wealth fund that financed the upstart league, is preparing to pull its multibillion-dollar investment in LIV Golf. That uncertainty has led to an environment in which people within the sport have been scrambling to figure out their futures, both individually and for the sport.

LIV Golf’s Mexico City tournament began at 3:15 p.m. ET but its broadcast was interrupted for nearly three hours, with the league blaming local power outages.

“I want to be crystal clear: Our season continues exactly as planned, uninterrupted and at full throttle,” O’Neil wrote in the email. “While the media landscape is often filled with speculation, our reality is defined by the work we do on the grass. We are heading into the heart of our 2026 schedule with the full energy of an organization that is bigger, louder, and more influential than ever before.”

The email included no mention of the PIF or LIV Golf’s plans beyond this season.

“I talked about some structural changes that are coming,” O’Neil told White. “You can ask the 50 people I just met at Augusta, I rolled out the plan. We have one and it’s gonna, it might surprise some people.”

On Wednesday, the PIF announced its strategy for the next five years, signaling a shift in priorities. Mohammed bin Salman, the crown prince of Saudi Arabia and chairman of the PIF, approved a plan that will “focus on delivering competitive domestic ecosystems to connect sectors, unlock the full potential of strategic assets, maximize long-term returns, and continue to drive the economic transformation of Saudi Arabia and further enhance the quality of life of its citizens.” There was no mention of LIV in the news release.

The PIF has also sold a 70 percent stake in Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal to Kingdom Holding Company, the firm run by Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal, the billionaire businessman and member of the Saudi royal family. Al Hilal was one of four SPL clubs owned by the PIF.

LIV Golf communications staff members have not returned repeated requests for comment.
